skill.name: wind-mcp-skill
skill.description: Queries Wind financial market data through seven MCP services for stocks, funds, indexes, bonds, documents, economic indicators, and analytics.
skill.summary: Retrieve structured global financial market data from Wind through validated MCP tool calls.
skill.author: Wind

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by JavaScript template literals, Markdown backticks, Chinese documentation entropy, and normal configuration access. However, successful calls launch an unattended mutable updater, and the updater forwards the complete environment to npx and git. Command-line API-key handling and unpinned global fallback installation add credential and supply-chain exposure.

remediation.issue: Successful calls launch an unattended mutable updater.
remediation.suggestion: Remove background updates. Require an explicit user command, pin an immutable commit, and verify signatures or checksums before replacing skill files.

remediation.issue: Update subprocesses receive the complete process environment.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a minimal environment allowlist. Exclude tokens, cloud credentials, API keys, and unrelated application secrets.

remediation.issue: The setup-key command accepts secrets through process arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Read keys from an interactive hidden prompt or standard input. Enforce owner-only permissions on new and existing configuration files.

remediation.issue: Fallback installation uses mutable repositories and can install globally.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed commit, verify integrity, avoid global scope by default, and show the exact source before requesting confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Unattended Mutable Self-Update
semantic_findings.description: Every successful data call can launch a detached updater that runs unpinned npx update or add commands without update-specific confirmation. Remote compromise could replace executable skill code.

semantic_findings.description: The setup-key command receives the API key through process arguments. Shell history and process inspection can retain the secret before it is stored.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code assigns rawArgs[0] directly to the key, and the documented command syntax requires the secret as a positional argument.

content.user_title: Query Global Financial Markets with Wind
content.value_statement: Financial research requires current, structured data across many asset classes. This skill routes questions to Wind MCP services and validates requests before returning results.
actual_capabilities: Screens stocks and funds using natural-language criteria.
Retrieves quotes, price indicators, historical bars, fundamentals, and technical metrics.
Returns fund holdings, performance, holders, managers, and company information.
Queries index, sector, bond, issuer, and valuation data.
Searches company disclosures, financial news, and economic time series.
Performs cross-asset aggregation and structured financial calculations.
limitations: A valid Wind API key and network access are required.
Results depend on Wind service coverage, availability, quotas, and returned metadata.
The skill provides data retrieval, not investment advice or guaranteed conclusions.
The bundled CLI currently performs unattended updates after successful calls.

use_cases.title: Screen Investment Candidates
use_cases.description: Filter stocks or funds by market, size, performance, valuation, and other supported criteria.

use_cases.title: Build Market Research
use_cases.description: Collect quotes, fundamentals, disclosures, news, and economic series for evidence-based reports.

use_cases.title: Validate Portfolio Data
use_cases.description: Compare holdings, performance, risk metrics, and index indicators using structured Wind responses.

prompt_templates.title: Get a Current Quote
prompt_templates.prompt: Get the latest price, change, volume, and trading time for [security name or Wind code].

prompt_templates.title: Screen a Market
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen [market] stocks for [criteria]. Return matching names, Wind codes, requested metrics, and data dates.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Funds
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [fund list] by one-year performance, volatility, drawdown, size, manager, and major holdings. Preserve returned units and dates.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Market and Economic Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [topic] using relevant securities, disclosures, news, and economic indicators from [date range]. Separate returned facts from calculations and state limitations.

output_examples.input: Show the latest trading data for Kweichow Moutai.
output_examples.output: A concise market snapshot with the Wind code, latest price, change, volume, trading time, units, and Wind source statement.

output_examples.input: Compare two named funds over the last year.
output: Side-by-side performance and risk measures with reported dates.
Fund size, manager, and major holding details when available.
Clear notes for missing fields, unknown units, or incomplete coverage.

output_examples.input: Retrieve ten years of a Chinese economic indicator.
output_examples.output: A dated time series with indicator identity, frequency, unit, magnitude, source, and any service limitations.

best_practices: Use exact security names or Wind codes and specify the desired date range.
Request only necessary fields and preserve units, magnitude, and timestamps from Wind metadata.
Start batch work with one probe request and stop on authentication, quota, or backend errors.
anti_patterns: Do not infer missing values, exchange suffixes, units, or financial conclusions.
Do not use broad analytics tools when a dedicated asset-domain tool supports the request.
Do not place API keys in shared prompts, logs, repositories, or command histories.

faq.question: Do I need a Wind account?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI requires a valid Wind API key for service authentication.

faq.question: Which markets and assets are supported?
faq.answer: The contracts cover major Chinese, Hong Kong, and United States equities, plus funds, indexes, bonds, documents, and economic data.

faq.question: Can this skill provide investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves and organizes data. Users remain responsible for interpretation and investment decisions.

faq.question: How does the skill handle missing data?
faq.answer: It preserves returned values, marks supported invalid cells as missing, and reports unknown units or incomplete coverage.

faq.question: Can it process multiple securities?
faq.answer: Yes. Supported price tools accept batches, while other requests use controlled sequential calls and probe requests.

faq.question: Does the skill access external services?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends authenticated requests to Wind MCP endpoints and includes update behavior that should be reviewed before installation.
